title: A Novel Sensitive and Stretchable TPU/MXene Film-Based Strain Sensor
content: The emergence of embodiment intelligence raises an immediate demand for high-performance strain sensors with adjustable large working ranges to enable precise deformation measurements. Herein, a high-performance strain sensor based on TPU/MXene composite films is fabricated via ultrasonic anchoring strategy, and its sensing mechanism is investigated based on piezoresistive effect. Benefiting from the synergistic sensing effect of the embedded conductive network constructed by ultrasonic anchoring and the reversible sliding behavior of surface conductive units, the proposed sensor successfully overcomes the narrow strain range limitation of conventional MXene-based strain sensors. The resulting TPU/MXene can achieve exceptional sensitivity (with a gauge factor up to 169.4) and reliable linearity (with R2 ≈ 0.99) across an ultra-wide strain range of 0 %–330 %, as well as stable signal output maintained after 1,000 tensile cycles. Besides, the optimized TPU/MXene sensor is successfully applied to monitor human joint movements including fingers, knees and throats. This work provides a feasible preparation strategy for high-stretchability and high-sensitivity MXene-based wearable strain sensors, and shows great application potential in human motion detection and rehabilitation monitoring of limb movements.
